title: Interpretations of the final shot in May December

commenti.body:
I just finished the movie. It is an interesting note. 

I haven’t really started analyzing it yet but there’s obviously a meta discussion about making a movie. Like earlier when she’s talking to the high schoolers, they ask her about sex scenes and she mentions all the people looking at you. How does that final scene start? With the shot of all the crew who are staring on as she’s in the process of starting this intimate moment.

She also mentions the line between pretending you’re feeling pleasure versus pretending you’re not feeling pleasure. And her last words during that scene are that it’s starting to feel more real.

There’s something there. 

That scene is artificial because we see all the filming info on screen. And the artificiality as the camera moves to film the scene. So I imagine whatever that change is for the fourth take has something to do with that idea of the metamorphosis into something real. 

The series is so deliberate, I don’t think the camera movement would be inconsequential.

Checking that scene again, I can't really imagine why that 4th take "just for me" is framed differently, but very clearly with the same camera. Of course the scene cuts just 2 seconds after the director calls "action" so as viewer we wouldn't really have any time to think about that detail before we're in the end credits. 

So I can't propose an answer to that question, and I'm not sure whether or not it's in any way consequential. It's certainly significant that her expression in that final shot is not in any way seductive or inviting, but cold and even hostile. 

Zooming out, I think there's a huge amount of ambiguity in that scene as following directly on from the "reveal" that Gracie-as-abuse-victim story is fake - or maybe not. The ambiguity is buzzing in the viewer's mind as the movie shoot begins, and we are now face to face with Elizabeth's belief that she really captured the character and the "truth" of the whole story.

Did she though? Or was she in fact too manipulative herself to get anywhere close to it? That the final shot is "just for me" \[i.e. Elizabeth\] as they are close to "getting more real" sets up the expectation that there really is a definitive interpretation of the Gracie-Joe affair that she can access and portray. But can there be when the principals themselves seem confused and conflicted as to what went on? 

That may be the reason for her bleak and blank expression in the final frame. She's drawn a blank in the interpretative process. OR she's ready to do a take of Gracie that's just openly sociopathic and manipulative. 

All of this of course ties in with the meta "melodrama-biopic" strand to the film. Which clearly needs digesting over more time and maybe more repeat views before it becomes coherent.

Excellent observation, though. Definitely worth mulling over.
